candidates.finding: Check whether two independent business-server processes concurrently acquiring the same workspace/session sandbox can produce duplicate or misattributed Docker ownership despite process-local key locks.
candidates.screening_result: Pinned current first-party KnowWork 033b492 Apache-2.0 already handles create-409 collision, but does not handle interprocess same-ID Docker start after a peer starts the container. The existing created-container and newly-created paths propagate Docker 304 as SandboxError; the latter can delete a running peer-used container. After preregistration, first-party native FakeDocker cases on independent dev-alpha-2 reproduce both failures RED, then 2/2 GREEN with bounded same-ID inspect-on-start-failure patch; full 34/34 lifecycle tests PASS with Python 3.12. This is deterministic interleaving evidence, not a real Docker multi-process test or observed production impact. External publication not executed.
candidates.observed_native_change: dev-alpha-2 pinned source 033b492: pristine control 08049ef5-2d7d-4632-bde2-c75f66518e7f six relevant PASS; regression-only RED dceb81f0-2561-4b29-a45e-abe6f757c279 two FAIL; fixed GREEN 7414d54d-b533-459f-8329-e72380074d41 two PASS; 7be843cc-5c20-45d9-b614-5815587ccef2 34/34 PASS; archived patches apply cleanly to clean source.

candidates.finding: Check whether a completed child continues consuming exported Registry child capacity or name while a safe supported replacement could be admitted.
candidates.screening_result: Current first-party Rune main 56828d7 Apache-2.0 static screen: Registry::create counts registered per-parent children, and Registry::remove explicitly removes from children and by_parent, freeing capacity; first-party test the_child_bound_is_per_parent_and_reports_limit_exceeded asserts replacement after remove. Completion closes child feedback but intentionally preserves it for parent transcript until explicit remove. The supported CLI uses a distinct Bridge/Runner flow: synchronous delegated read-only child and an atomic count of delegations against SubagentChildren; these are lifetime-session budget semantics rather than a demonstrated stuck terminal slot. No supported automatic reclaim obligation or native adverse case identified; speculative auto-removal could break transcript ownership, so no patch. Read-only static screen; no native tests run.

candidates.finding: Check whether a terminated task-bound worker can strand the conditional TaskStore ownership claim so supported worker reassignment is blocked without safe reclaim.
candidates.screening_result: At exact assessed/default first-party source e48780b, MIT: TeamCoordinator.spawn claims a task before Popen and rolls it back on OSError; worker heartbeat occurs only from a POST_TOOL_USE hook, throttled to one per 60 seconds. TaskStore.reclaim_stale deliberately skips every in_progress task with no last_heartbeat_at, to avoid reclaiming main-agent/manual tasks. Native isolated stdlib TaskStore probe on dev-alpha-2 (session f13d8416-9a03-4c78-b42e-63998a0d4444, exit 0) reproduces a pre-first-heartbeat claimed task remaining in_progress after reclaim_stale/find_ready and refusing a replacement owner. The probe models an abrupt death by absence of heartbeat; it does not terminate a real worker. Existing healthy-heartbeat reclaim exists. Need actual supported worker process lifecycle/ownership and safe terminal evidence before reclaiming no-heartbeat tasks.
candidates.blocker: No first-party supported proof that a no-heartbeat claimed owner is dead (rather than main/manual agent or a silent but active worker), nor a safe atomic PID/lifecycle claimant check before reset. Determine native worker termination and reassignment semantics, then test stale owner vs live owner and race with heartbeat; do not simply reclaim every no-heartbeat claim.

candidates.finding: Check whether simultaneous same-tenant same-run NodeService.start calls launch duplicate S1 runs before a single idempotent registry entry is established.
candidates.screening_result: At exact assessed/default first-party source a675849 MIT: NodeService.start acquires self.lock before reading (ctx.tenant, run_id), creates one recorder/cancel/done entry and stores it under that lock, and releases lock only before spawning its worker thread; a competing same-tenant same-run call necessarily sees the entry and returns started=False. Tenant context is part of both map key and sandbox name. Existing first-party contract test covers separate tenants with same ID. No gap fitting the prespecified same-instance simultaneous-start duplication hypothesis; read-only static control-path screen, not a native parallel stress test. Cross-process workers are outside this process-local service contract and were not claimed in this hypothesis.

candidates.finding: Check whether concurrent shared-thread turns with colliding provider-local tool-call IDs can misattribute a peer result during stitchHistory repair.
candidates.screening_result: Pinned first-party current main 3beb3d6 Apache-2.0 has stitchHistory resultFor Map keyed only by raw callId with last-write-wins. Independent dev-alpha-2 cached Node 22 Docker run (session 87e1aa54-5794-4ef9-9140-8d1133c0a15a, no network/LLM) executes exact source-native history.ts: two assistant calls both id c1 and two distinct replies are stitched into beta-result, beta-result, alpha-result, expected native diagnostic RED/exit 1. A real shared-thread duplicate ID collision has not been observed in production; raw Message schema lacks a distinct owner key. A bounded repair that can unambiguously associate call with result in arbitrary interleavings has not been established, so hold without patch or external benefit claim.
candidates.blocker: Need safe, first-party supported per-call/turn provenance or explicit fail-closed duplicate-ID policy and provider adapter compatibility; completion order cannot reliably identify owners. Confirm real duplicate-ID input path, add collision/ordinary-history native tests and establish nonlossy policy before authoring a patch.
